subject: compare high-price markets without blanket verdicts
preheader: los angeles, san diego, seattle, and new york still require property-level evidence.
headline: A metro label does not decide a property's economics.
body: For a Los Angeles address, verify the asking price, achievable property-specific rent, parcel tax, insurance, local rules, condition, expenses, and written financing terms. Do not import an uncited metro median into the property model.
Apply the same process in San Diego. Similar headlines do not make two properties or submarkets financially equivalent, and a rent-to-price shortcut omits operating costs and financing.
For Seattle, separate current observed income and expenses from employment, appreciation, and rent-growth scenarios. Record a dated source for every forward assumption.

For a New York City property, obtain unit-, building-, and jurisdiction-specific legal and operating review, including any condominium, cooperative, rent-regulation, tax, insurance, and financing constraints that actually apply.
TrueCap can organize a preliminary screen from editable assumptions. It does not establish that a market is broken, predict appreciation, resolve local law, or tell you to buy, hold, or walk.
